defects: The hypothesis `∃! (p : M × M), p.1 ∈ f.support ∧ p.2 ∈ g.support ∧ p.1 * p.2 = a0 * b0` only asserts existence of a unique factorizing pair somewhere, but never requires that pair to equal (a0, b0). The gold's `UniqueMul f.coeff.support g.coeff.support a0 b0` specifically forces any such factorizing pair to equal (a0, b0). These are not equivalent: one can construct f, g, a0, b0 where the produced hypothesis holds (unique pair is some (a1,b1) ≠ (a0,b0) with a1*b1 = a0*b0) while a0 ∉ supp f, making the conclusion (f*g)(a0*b0) = f(a0)*g(b0) false (LHS nonzero via the (a1,b1) term, RHS zero). Hence the produced theorem as stated is not even true in general.

Typeclass assumption is strengthened from gold's `[Mul A]` to `[Monoid M]`, adding unnecessary identity/associativity requirements not present in the gold statement, narrowing the class of types the theorem applies to.
